answer: The protocol validates 1,000 unique location proofs by measuring signal transit across a rugged cedar grid to enforce physical presence. An issuer assigns geographic coordinates as a spatial beacon, and each receipt proves an agent physically occupied the site. A verifier functions as a secure vault, replaying logs to detect latency shifts; any discrepancy beyond the noise floor triggers a permanent penalty. Honest nodes pay linear physical travel costs to reach sites, while 1,000 fake identities incur unsustainable signal congestion without relay help.
